title: Weight intersections and joint geometric level
as_he_states: It is not tautological that two weight presentations give their intersection; joint weight/level is stronger than the conjunction.

state_of_art: WeilII3.4.1 gives unique numerical weights. Grothendieck1969 distinguishes effective Hodge structures from geometric support. No exact all-purpose identification of the source geometric joint class was found.
why_open: The pages identify the existential-filtration difficulty; no source states why the programme was later abandoned.
worth: High mathematical interest but only definition comparison and low-dimensional cases fit one research run.

as_he_states: The local bound improves to min(i,2n−1−i), with a top-piece claim whose verb differs between transcriptions.

Durfee–Saito1990Thm4.1 proves link intersection-cohomology weight estimates with different dimensions/supports. Double blowup obstructs the strong identification. The derived MHS spectral-sequence step is checked using Saito1989 Theorems1.3–1.4 and Kebekus–Schnell Proposition9.2, then restricting the finite weight filtration to the proper fibre; no degeneration is needed. This supplies the compatibility left unchecked in Hua2026 p36/Problem3, not the separate geometric-level assertion.
why_open: No historical abandonment evidence; the prior notes conflated a mathematical survival assertion with the Pro verb.
worth: High interest and feasible in one run as a carefully scoped local-Hodge exposition after the scan check.

title: One or two primes detect smooth motives
as_he_states: One invertible prime, or two distinct primes on their invertibility loci, should detect all-prime smoothness.
plausible_today: NOS answers the abelianH¹/trait case. Any generalization must specify the motive category, compatible system, normal base and residue-characteristic exclusions.
state_of_art: Serre–Tate1968Theorem1 is the precise good-reduction criterion; Vasiu–Zink shows that all-prime unramifiedness still does not imply object extension over arbitrary regular mixed-characteristic bases. No exact broad independence theorem found in recorded searches.
why_open: No published source explains why this exact manuscript formulation was dropped; do not infer a solution from compatibility alone.
worth: High conceptual interest, but one run should produce an exact case table and dependency list.

title: Geometric level and standard-conjectural motives
as_he_states: The weight/level programme presupposes motivic and semisimplicity inputs; the attached introduction B12-01 says the structures should exist motivically and be l-independent.
plausible_today: Separate numerical weights, Hodge types, algebraic generation, numerical motives, homological motives and motivated cycles before making any unconditional identification.
state_of_art: JannsenTheorem1 proves numerical pure semisimplicity, not numerical=homological. Arapura6.4.1 compares pure Nori with André; Choudhury–Gallauer9.1 compares Nori/Ayoub Hopf algebras. None proves algebraicity of all motivated correspondences. October2026 preprints claim CM rational/generalized Hodge and consequences for finite-field abelian Tate and arbitrary-characteristic abelian Hodge-standard. Milne’s9November report treats these as theorems. This run inspected the precise statements, not the full new proof; general varieties and integral cycle surjectivity remain outside this update.
why_open: The supplied introduction explicitly calls the motivic framework conjectural; no later comparison is evidence that all its standard conjectures are solved.
worth: Highest conceptual value as a dependency map shared with root; a few hours can clarify scope, not settle cycle conjectures.
